evidence: host/owner-host.lisp:1313-1318: `(if memory (value (fn-ores-config-refused memory)) (let ((state (f-put-global 'fn-owner-connection-held (fn-cbud-deltas-held v gen stamp deltas held) state))) (fn-owner-reconfigure-deltas-admitted id deltas fn-arena state)))`. books/connection-budget.lisp:757 makes the held slots `(max (nfix (fn-cbud-held-at 8 held)) ...)`. fn-owner-reconfigure-deltas-admitted (1270-1273) can still refuse after this write (fn-ocfg-reconfig-refusal, or the fn-cca-preflight :ok test), and fn-owner-reconfigure-unstage (1523-1528) never restores the value.
fix: Compute the candidate held value, but write fn-owner-connection-held only when the stage actually staged a record. Better still, write it at fn-owner-reconfigure-complete for the published generation, and restore or drop it on unstage. Recompute the slots from the published configuration instead of taking a monotone max.
notes: 10-02 23:22 escalate: fix lives in host/owner-host.lisp (forbidden zone)
reviewer: The ratchet is real. fn-owner-reconfigure-deltas (owner-host.lisp:1313-1318) writes held before fn-owner-reconfigure-deltas-admitted, which can still refuse at 1270-1273 (fn-cca-preflight). fn-owner-reconfigure-unstage (1523-1528) never restores held. fn-cbud-deltas-slots takes the max (books/connection-budget.lisp:757). This is a documented, deliberate choice: connection-budget.lisp:787-789 says "Taken at the check, before the staging's durable write: a staging that then fails leaves a charge at most larger than needed, never smaller." It fails safe, refusing too much rather than admitting too much. The effect is spurious :connections-exceed-memory refusals until restart after a refused large handshake setting. That is an availability nuisance, not a soundness hole.
scenario: An operator runs `policy set tls-handshakes-in-flight 4096`. The memory check passes, so held becomes 4096 slots. The staging step then refuses (preflight refusal on a node with a consumer position), or the live request is unstaged after authorization fails. The configuration still says the old value, but fn-owner-connection-held keeps the 4096-slot scratch for the rest of the run. Lowering the row later cannot reduce it, because the slots are a max. Every later reconfiguration that raises max-connections is refused :connections-exceed-memory, against handshake scratch that no live configuration can use, until the process restarts.
title: Connection memory charge is ratcheted before the reconfiguration is admitted, and never released
